Shene zecharim ushete nekevot. safek hen, deshemma kol chada yalda zachar unekeva, veshemma hannekevot yatzu techilla, hilkach en lakkohen kan kelum, ella mafrish alehem shene telaim leafkoe leissurayhu vehen leatzman, kach pershu rabbotay. aval rambam savar deen kan lakkohen kelum vaafillu tale leatzmo eno tzarich lehaferish, mishshum deikka vechol chad mehanach sefeke tuva kesheyyaldu shete nekevot vezachar, shemma achat mishshetehen yalda shete nekevot vehaacheret zachar, o shemma zo yalda nekeva vehaacheret zachar veacharav nekeva, o nekeva veachareha zachar. vechen sefekot harebe yesh bishne zecharim ushete nekevot, hilkach afillu tale leatzmo eno mafrish. uferush rabbotay ikkar:

Shilluach hakken. aval lo vemukdashin. mashkachat mukdashin deillu hayu chullin hayu chayyavim beshilluach hakken, kegon shehaya lo of vehikdisho keshehu virshuto levedek habbayit, uvarach, umetzao achar kach rovetz al hakken vehikkiro. i nammi, kegon shehikdish gozalot shel shovacho lammizbeach leolat nedava, veachar kach kesheggadlu otan gozalot barchu veyatzu vekinnenu bemakom acher, demeikkara ki akdeshinhu dideh havu vechal hekdesh alayhu, vehasheta dimtzaan lav mezumman hu, vei havu chullin havu michayyeve:
Veeno noheg ella vesheeno mezumman. dichtiv ki yikkare, perat limzumman:
Shekkinnenu vefardes. shemmardu veyatzu min habbayit, veenan chozrot labbayit, venaasu midbariyyot. ufardes lav mezumman hu mippene sheyyecholot livroach:
Haredsiot. sheddarkan liggadel im bene adam. veal shem hordos hammelech shehaya mitassek begiddulan nikreu haredsiot al shemo:
Derusat ish. beulat ish:

Neemenet. velo hifsida ketubbatah. umikkol makom i eshet kohen hi uleachar zeman haerusin keshennissea taan derusat ish at, mappekinan lah minneh, deshemma leachar sheeras otah nivala, umikki amar derusat ish at shavya annafsheh chaticha deissura. vaafillu nivala beones, ha kayma lan eshet kohen shenneensa asura levaalah. umegaresh lah veyahev lah ketubbatah:

Haevar vehabbasar hameduldalim bivhema. nitlash mimmenna evar dehaynu basar vegidim vaatzamot, o nitlash mimmenna basar levaddo, vaadayin hen meurin bah bemiktzat. veyesh hefresh ben evar min hachay levasar min hachay, shehaevar metamme adam vechelim kinvela, vehabbasar sheeno evar, tahor mikkelum, kidyalfinan mikkera dichtiv (Vayikra 11) vechi yamut min habbehema, mimmiktzat behema kegon evar mimmenna, vesefa dikra hannogea benivlatah yitma, umiddichtiv vechi yamut mashma keen mita bainan sheenah osa chalifin, laafoke basar sheose chalifin, sheim yitlosh basar min habbehema, basar acher ole tachtav:

Metammein tumat ochalin. im chashav alehen lehaachilan lenachri, havu ochel lekabbel tuma uletamme acherim. detumat atzman en bahen ad sheyyittalshu chullan, aval mekabbelin tuma min hashsheretz umetammein bah et acherim:
Utzerichim hechsher. lavo vammayim leachar shenniddaldelu, veachar kach mekabbelim tuma leolam:
Nishchata habbehema. nitharu milletamme od mishshum nevela. veaf al pi sheasurim baachila mishshum uvasar bassade terefa, yede nevela taharu, deen shechita osa nippul:
Huchsheru vedameha. lekabbel tuma belo hechsher acher, kedin behema shennishchata veyatza mimmenna dam shehuchshar besarah beoto dam:

Meta habbehema habbasar. shenniddaldel: tzarich hechsher. lekabbel tuma min hashsheretz im lo huchshar mishshenniddaldel. detumat nevela en bo, demita osa nippul venechshav keillu nafal oto haevar o oto habbasar hameduldal veeno naase nevela immah bemitatah, ella keillu feresh mechayyim hu, uvasar happoresh min hachay tahor:

Haevar metamme mishshum evar min hachay. demita osa nippul kidfareshna, veeno naase nevela immah, hilkach eno metamme mishshum nevela. veikka ben evar min hachay leevar min hannevela, devasar happoresh meevar min hachay lo metamme, shehare afillu basar happoresh min hachay lo metamme, kol shekken basar happoresh meevar min hachay, veillu basar happoresh meevar min hannevela metamme kevasar happoresh min hannevela atzmah:

Verabbi shimon metaher. i efshar leokme milleteh derabbi shimon ahach desefa, demimma nafshach, i mita osa nippul littame mishshum evar min hachay, vei enah osa nippul littame mishshum evar min nevela. hilkach al karchacha rabbi shimon aresha kae, haevar vehabbasar hameduldalim babbehema metammein tumat ochalin bimkoman, verabbi shimon metaher haevar kol zeman shemmeure bevaale chayyim sheeno metamme tumat ochalin. vetaama derabbi shimon, deamar kera (Vayikra 11) mikkol haochel asher yeachel, ochel sheatta yachol lehaachilo lenachri behetter karuy ochel umetamme tumat ochalim, laafoke haevar vehabbasar hameduldalim sheasurim lannachri mishum evar min hachay umishshum basar min hachay, sheenan keruyin ochel veen metammein tumat ochalim. vahalacha kerabbi meir bishtehen:

rashi: Lemaan telech. musav al hammikra shellemala lehatztzilecha midderech raa, lemaan holichecha bederech tovim:
targum: Bedil halech bearchata detave ushevile detzadike tintor:

rashi: Ki yesharim yishkenu aretz. laolam habba:
Yivvateru vah. kesheyyeredu reshaim legehinnom:
targum: Metul ditritze omdin beara veilen dela mum mishtoterin bah:
Verashiaya min ara nesufun uvazoze nitakrun minah:

Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 4:16-27: There was an incident concerning a man who was standing in the synagogue with his son standing opposite him; and while all the people were responding "Hallelujah" after [the reading of] the ark, his son was responding with idle words. They said to him: look at your son, who is answering with idle words! He said to them: what shall I do with him - he is a child, let him play. The next day he did the same, and throughout all eight days of the festival, and he said nothing to him. Before one year, or two years, or three years had passed, that man died, and his wife died, and his son died, and his son's son died, and fifteen souls went forth from his household, and only one pair remained to him - one lame and blind, the other a fool and wicked.

Again, there was an incident concerning a man who used to regret that he had not read [Scripture] or studied [Mishnah]. Once he was standing in the synagogue, and when the one passing before the ark reached the sanctification of the [Divine] Name, he raised his voice and said, "Holy, holy, holy." They said to him: why did you raise your voice? He said to them: I did not merit [to learn] Scripture or Mishnah, and now that permission has been given to me [to say this], shall I not raise my voice, that my soul may find satisfaction? Before that year, or two, or three years had passed, that man went up from Babylonia to the Land of Israel, and they made him the general of Caesar's army, and appointed him head over all the fortresses in the Land of Israel, and gave him a place, and he built a city and settled in it, and it was called "Colonia" after him, for him and his children and his children's children forever.

There was an incident concerning a certain priest who fed his animal terumah [priestly tithe], and fire fell upon him and consumed from him thirty stacks of grain, thirty garments, twenty-four jars of wine, sixteen jars of oil, and other property he had. He came and stood before the Sages and told them what had happened to him. He said to them: I am a priest, and I fed my animal terumah. The Sages heard and said: blessed is the Omnipresent, who shows no favoritism! For does not terumah and consecrated produce that have no eaters go only to be burned? He said to them: but did you not teach me that vetches of terumah may be fed to cattle, wild animals, and chickens? They said to him: they only permitted this regarding vetches which are, from the outset, animal food, and which people eat [only] in a year of famine - therefore David decreed concerning them [that they be treated more leniently]. From here they said: whoever feeds his animal terumah, even terumah from outside the Land, of him Scripture says (Proverbs 19:16), "he who despises his ways shall die," and it says (Numbers 18:32), "and you shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel," and so on.

We learn from Abraham that from the beginning of his deeds he feared before the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said (Genesis 15:1), "fear not, Abram" - for one says "fear not" only to one who truly fears Heaven. They gave a parable for this: to what may this be compared? To a king who said to his son, go forth and kill these bandits, and if they fall into your hand, do not benefit from their wealth, so that people should not say the king's son went forth to kill these bandits only to seize their wealth. He went forth and killed them; on his return, his father went out to meet him and said to him: my son, blessed are you, and may you have satisfaction of mind that you took no benefit at all from their wealth, and now I will pay you from my own treasury - silver, gold, precious stones, pearls, and every desirable object in the world. For this reason our father Abraham was compared [to this]: at the time he killed the kings, the king of Sodom went out to meet him and said to him, "give me the persons," and so on [Genesis 14:21]. He said to him: fool of the world! Do I need silver, gold, precious stones, pearls, and every desirable object of yours - from a thread to a shoelace [I will not take anything of yours]? For this reason it is said, "I am your shield," and so on.

We learn from Isaac that from the beginning of his deeds he feared before the Holy One, blessed be He. Isaac was seventy-five years old at the time our father Abraham passed away. He said: woe is me, perhaps I do not have good deeds such as my father had - what will become of me before the Holy One, blessed be He? Immediately the mercy of the Holy One, blessed be He, was stirred, and He spoke with him that very night, as it is said (Genesis 25:11), "and it came to pass after the death of Abraham," and so on.

We learn from Jacob that from the beginning of his deeds he feared Heaven, as it is said (ibid. 35:4), "and they gave to Jacob all the foreign gods," and so on. And likewise our first forefathers, as it is said (Exodus 14:31), "and Israel saw the great hand," and so on - to teach you that as a reward for the fear and the faith with which they believed in Him at first, the Holy One, blessed be He, will in the future come and redeem them, as it is said (Micah 4:10), "writhe and labor to bring forth, O daughter of Zion," and so on - to this point.

Regarding the matter of the fear of sin, Rashbi, peace be upon him, further explained (Zohar, Bereshit 7b), in these words: "why is it called 'the fear of the LORD'? Because it [Malchut] is the Tree of Good and Evil - if a person merits, behold, good; and if he does not merit, behold, evil; and therefore fear rests in this place, and it is the gate above to all the good of the world" - to this point.

The intent of his asking "why is it called the fear of the LORD" is to raise two questions: first, concerning the very existence of fear in this place [Malchut]; and second, what is the connection to the two words "fear of the LORD," rather than saying "fear of God"? And he answered: "because it is the Tree of Good and Evil." My teacher, peace be upon him, explained, in his commentary on the Sabba, that this attribute [Malchut] is called the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil because it draws from the depth of good and the depth of evil, which are kindness and judgment; and further, that beneath it are good and evil, as is explained in the Tikkunim (90b): "the Tree of the Knowledge of good - this is Metatron; and evil - this is Samael." And Scripture says (Deuteronomy 30:15), "see, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil" - life is bound with good, and death is bound with evil, and two paths branch out from it [Malchut] below, and therefore this is the place of [free] choice, and it is written, "and you shall choose life." And if a person merits through his deeds, he cleaves to the good, which is "the LORD," the Tree of Life, which is the side of kindness and mercy - namely (Psalms 145:9), "the LORD is good to all, and His mercies are over all His works" - and likewise "the LORD" [in gematria] adds up to "TOV" [good] with the kolel; and if he does not merit, he cleaves to the evil, which is death, namely the external husks [kelipot].

With this both points of grammar are resolved: one must fear because beneath it is evil, lest his soul cleave to evil - for death and the evil to which it cleaves become the portion of his soul after his departure from the world, in the manner explained in the Zohar (Parashat Korach 177a), on the verse (Job 34:11), "for the work of a man He will render to him." And likewise, one should not cause this attribute [Malchut] to cleave to evil, Heaven forfend, as will be further explained concerning the blemish a person causes to the [divine] attributes, blessed be He. And likewise "the fear of the LORD" - for if one fears, he merits to cleave to "the LORD," which is good, and his soul, after its departure from the world, cleaves to the good - namely, the good that is hidden away for the righteous in the Garden of Eden - "and God saw the light, that it was good," for "the LORD" is the source of all the good in the world; and this he examined closely by saying, "this is the gate to enter into all the good of the world." And the word "good" follows the principle that "there is nothing higher than delight" [oneg]; also, the word "good" comprises all the good found in all the [divine] attributes, this being "the LORD," the totality of the ten attributes in direct light, which is kindness and mercy, as is explained in the Tikkunim (6b).

Now, man is composed of good and evil, which are the good inclination and the evil inclination; and if a person merits to subdue the evil inclination within him, he causes the subduing of the [forces of] judgment and the husks, and causes the drawing forth of good upon himself - and this is what is meant by the precise wording "if a person merits" - for a person is composed of good and evil, and must strengthen the good inclination over the evil inclination; and if, Heaven forfend, he does the opposite, he blemishes the supernal roots, for judgment is not comprised under kindness [when it dominates].

This is explained in the Zohar (Va'era 26b), on the verse (Deuteronomy 4:39), "and you shall know this day, and take it to your heart" - in these words: "Rabbi Elazar further said: the wicked cause a blemish above. What is this blemish? That the left is not comprised within the right - that the evil inclination is not comprised within the good inclination, because of the sins of mankind; and the blemish they cause affects only themselves, as it is written (ibid. 32:5), 'He has become corrupted, not His children, the blemish is theirs' - as it were, they act, and yet they do not act: they act, so that the blessings from above are not drawn down upon them, as it is said (ibid. 11:17), 'and He will restrain the heavens, and there will be no rain'; and they do not act, for the heavens themselves take for themselves the blessings they need, and do not take them to draw them down below - and certainly the blemish belongs to those wicked ones. Further, [the word] 'lo' [not, spelled with a Vav in this reading] indicates that the right is not comprised within the left, so that blessings are not drawn down below; [the word] 'lo' [with an Alef, meaning 'to Him'] indicates that they do not take [the blessings] to draw them down below. Who causes this? Because the wicked separate the evil inclination from the good inclination and cleave to the evil inclination" - to the extent relevant here.

Our intent in citing this is clear, but nevertheless let us explain the matter of the blemish he mentioned, "they act, and yet they do not act." The intent is that Rabbi Elazar found the plain sense of the verse difficult: for if, as it appears, "He has become corrupted, not" - meaning that no blemish reaches Him, blessed be He, from our deeds, but rather "His children, their blemish" - that the blemish and the flaw are in the children who commit that blemish and sin - if so, the verse should simply have said "His children, their blemish, a perverse and crooked generation," [without the intervening word]. Therefore he explained that the intent of "He has become corrupted" is that a blemish does reach Him, but it is not a complete blemish - this is [the meaning of] "lo" spelled with an Alef [merely "to Him," a partial effect]; but the complete blemish and flaw is in the children who commit it - "His children, their blemish" [mumam]. Therefore, regarding what pertains to Him, it says "shichet" [corrupted], which is a minor corruption, but what pertains to the children is a complete "mum" [blemish]. With this we may understand the words of Rabbi Elazar, peace be upon him, who said "the wicked cause a blemish above," and so on, and then said "and the blemish they cause affects only themselves" - that the actual blemish is in them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 4:28-40: He explains the matter of the blemish, saying: "they act, so that the blessings from above are not drawn down upon them, as in 'and He will restrain the heavens, and there will be no rain.'" The intent is that it is the way of the supernal heavens to bestow good flow and mercy upon the lower beings, and the Holy One, blessed be He, must restrain them from bestowing in their usual way - as it is written, "and He will restrain the heavens" - and from this a certain blemish comes upon "the heavens," in the manner explained in the Zohar (Balak 197a), on the verse (Song of Songs 1:8), "if you do not know, O fairest among women" - that Malchut is called "Atzeret" [restraint], for she gathers in all the supernal flow that comes to her, and she restrains it, giving to the lower beings only drop by drop, because they are unworthy. In these words, in brief: "and when it reaches her, all that she has gathered, she restrains, withholds, and delays, so that it comes down only like dew, drop by drop. Why? Because she does not find faith below as she finds above, [where] it is poured out on every side without delay, and she rejoices, and then they give her many gifts and bounties, one upon another, and they do not delay her at all. But the lower beings delay them, and delay her, and then she is 'Atzeret,' restrained, held back; certainly, as it were, she gives [only] a residue, and no more" - to the extent relevant here.

In this manner a blemish reaches "the heavens," in that they must be restrained against their own way, and from this distress comes to them - like the parable of a generous, open-handed man: if his hand is held back from giving, distress undoubtedly comes to him. "And they do not act" - "for the heavens take for themselves" - meaning that they are full of flow and blessing for their own needs, and the complete blemish that reaches the lower beings is that they receive nothing at all; this is [the meaning of] "and they do not take to draw it down below" - certainly, "the blemish is theirs," the wicked - and this is what they themselves caused.

Further, "lo" spelled with a Vav [indicating] that the right is not comprised within the left - now he explains a further blemish that reaches above, in a manner different from what was said, saying that the right is not comprised within the left, so that the right should not be included with the left to subdue judgment, because the lower beings separate the evil inclination from the good inclination. And he said, "so that blessings are not drawn down to the lower beings" - returning to the first explanation, for the two matters are one; and therefore he did not say "another interpretation" but "further" - meaning an additional point beyond what was said, yet both are [essentially] the same.

Now that a person knows that his situation is not like that of the other nations, the seventy nations - for whom, whether the good inclination prevails over the evil inclination or the reverse, their situation makes no difference [above], since they did not accept the whole Torah - but Israel, who are called children to the Omnipresent and are called "Adam," as it is said (Ezekiel 34:31), "you are Adam," and were created in the supernal image, as it is said (Genesis 9:6), "in the image of God He made man" - whatever they do affects the supernal roots, from the aspect of the soul within them, and the good inclination and evil inclination flow into them from above, as is explained in the Zohar (Bereshit 49a) - that they are the secret of the two arms, see there; and further there (ibid.), on the verse (Genesis 3:6), "and the woman saw that the tree was good for food." Therefore one must always fear lest he blemish himself - that is, his soul - through the removal of the supernal light from it; and this is [the meaning of] "his children, their blemish." For even though one might interpret "and He will restrain the heavens, and there will be no rain" as referring to physical rain - this would fit in years of famine, but if one sins in years of plenty, how would "and He will restrain the heavens" be fulfilled? Rather, it certainly refers to the withholding of the light of Torah from the souls below - for the Torah is compared to rain, as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:2), "my teaching shall drip as the rain," and so on, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Ta'anit 7a); and likewise in the Tikkunim, "there is no rain except the flow of Torah."

Thus one must fear lest he cause a blemish above, as I have explained, and therefore must always strengthen the good inclination over the evil inclination. And besides this, one must strengthen the side of kindness and mercy over judgment, such as the qualities of compassion, acts of loving-kindness, and the like - all of which flow from the good inclination, which is the side of kindness - and remove from his heart the qualities of cruelty, vengeance, anger, and envy, all of which are qualities flowing from the evil inclination, whose root is the root of judgment.

The way for a person to acquire fear in his heart is to subdue the husks [kelipot] and strengthen the good inclination over the evil inclination; and this Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, taught us in the verse (Deuteronomy 10:12), "and now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you, but to fear," where he said (ibid. 10:16), "and you shall circumcise the foreskin of your heart" - and it is known that the foreskin derives from the evil inclination; and since he called it "foreskin," we understand that the evil inclination has the laws of "orlah" [the foreskin of fruit, forbidden for three years] applied to it - "for three years it shall be forbidden [foreskinned] to you" - and it is explained in the Tikkunim (10b) that these three years correspond to the three shells of the walnut.

And it is known that to eat the kernel of the walnut one must break the shells; therefore the prophets outside the Land, before reaching holiness, had to break through the shell: (Ezekiel 1:4), "and I looked, and behold, a stormy wind came out of the north" - this is one; "a great cloud" - two; "and a fire flaring up" - three; "and a brightness was about it" - this is the fourth, thin shell that is eaten together with the walnut, and from within it the likeness of the four Chayot [living creatures], which are the four compartments found within the walnut.

And likewise these three shells are mentioned in the words concerning Elijah, as it is said (I Kings 19:11), "and behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rending mountains and breaking rocks in pieces before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind; and after the wind an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake; and after the earthquake a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire; and after the fire, a still, small voice." My teacher, peace be upon him, explained in Sefer HaPardes that although the husks [kelipot] number ten, their roots are three, corresponding to the three shells of the walnut mentioned. From this we learn that although the qualities of the evil inclination are many, their roots are three, being three shells upon the evil inclination in the heart - and yet they are [ultimately] one, as we shall explain.

The first is pride, corresponding to "a great and strong wind" - and without doubt pride is the root of all evil qualities, as we shall elaborate, with God's help, in its own Gate. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (69b), that the heart is like the walnut, which has shells and a foreskin, in these words: "and the coarseness of the heart, which rules over its own shells and is not broken - of it is said (Proverbs 16:5), 'every haughty heart is an abomination to the LORD,' and the Shechinah does not rest upon it; and from the side of the shells, people are called 'uncircumcised of heart'" - to this point.

The second, corresponding to the hard shell of the walnut, is a person's stiffness of neck; and therefore Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, said (Deuteronomy 10:16), "and you shall circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and stiffen your neck no more" - and this too is a quality flowing from pride.

The third is a person's boiling over in anger and harsh speech, including inflaming himself with the fire of the [evil] inclination to commit a transgression - this corresponds to "a fire flaring up," and this too is a quality flowing from pride, namely "the coarseness of the heart which rules over its own shells" - for the coarseness of the heart has these three shells mentioned, all of which spring from it.

I heard from the honorable Rabbi Avraham HaLevi that the reason it says of these three, "not in the wind of the LORD, not in the earthquake of the LORD, not in the fire of the LORD," is that the Shechinah does not rest in these three; rather, "in the still, small voice - there the King comes." And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (3b). And it is likewise the way of the members of an earthly king's palace to speak in a hushed manner, and one whose words are spoken in a low voice follows the ways of humility, and undoubtedly cleaves to the King, as we shall write concerning humility, with God's help.

This is the aspect of inner fear: that a person should always consider that he is before the King, and fear before Him, and not raise his voice before Him; and this is what is explained in the Tikkunim (ibid.), "'a still, small voice' - this is the Yud" - although it is expounded there for a different purpose, nevertheless, for our purposes, since we explained above that the secret of fear is the Yud, we may learn what is needed to acquire fear: that it should be in a still, small voice, and that one should keep far from the three shells of pride, which are "a great wind," "an earthquake," and "a fire."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 4:41-52: It may be that this is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, intended in saying (Proverbs 8:13), "the fear of the LORD is to hate evil; pride, and arrogance, and the evil way, and the perverse mouth, I hate." For in order to merit the fear of the LORD, which is the good hidden away, the kernel of the walnut, one must break and crush the foreskin, which is the evil, and distance himself from it so much that it becomes hated and loathsome for him to draw near it; and this is "to hate evil" - the husks and evil in general are these three: "pride, and arrogance, and the evil way," and so on, which are the three shells of the walnut I explained, being the root of evil.

Now, a person merits to break these husks by separating himself from the pleasures of the world, all of which derive from the husks of the serpent's foreskin and the evil inclination; and this is [the meaning of] (Psalms 34:10), "fear the LORD, His holy ones, for those who fear Him lack nothing." And Ramban, peace be upon him, explained (Parashat Kedoshim) that every expression of holiness refers to a person's separation and restraint from the desires of the world, and the restraining of his speech and the like; and I shall cite his words, with God's help, in the matters that lead to humility, one of which is holiness.

Likewise one must be careful of every negative commandment in the Torah, for whoever breaches the fence of a negative commandment causes the evil serpent to enter within; and this is [the meaning of] "fearing God and turning away from evil" (Job 1:8). And so said King David, peace be upon him (Psalms 34:12-15), "come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD. Who is the man who desires life, who loves days to see good? Keep your tongue from evil," and so on, "turn from evil and do good." And the reason he juxtaposed to fear "who is the man who desires life" is that the fear of the LORD is a source of life, as I explained above at the end of chapter two.

The matter of "turn from evil and do good" is the fear that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the passage we cited above from Parashat Bereshit (7b), "because it is the Tree of Good and Evil - if a person merits, behold, good; if he does not merit, behold, evil." Therefore it says "turn from evil" - to distance oneself from evil to the utmost degree of distance; and so said King Solomon, peace be upon him (Proverbs 14:16), "a wise man fears and turns away from evil."

The reason is as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Avot 4:2): "one commandment leads to another commandment, and one transgression leads to another transgression." The pious Rabbi Yosef Yaavetz explained, in his commentary on this Mishnah, that the commandments flow from the Tree of Life and are spiritual entities cleaving to Him, blessed be He; and one who performs a commandment cleaves to Him, blessed be He, and the more commandments he adds, the more cleaving he adds - so that one commandment leads to another commandment, and the reward of a commandment is [another] commandment, in the manner of "the sanctuary itself: when consecrated from below, it is consecrated from above" - this is the abbreviated sense of his intent. And this is [the meaning of] "if a person merits, behold, good" - for the good to which he cleaves becomes his portion; and if, Heaven forfend, he cleaves to evil, the evil becomes his portion, and he is destined to do many evil things. And so the pious one, of blessed memory, explained there concerning "and flees from transgression" - that he flees as one who sees before him a great bonfire of wood, from which he must distance himself by a bowshot. I found support for this explanation in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, cited in the Yalkut (Mishlei, remez 959), on the verse (Proverbs 19:2), "also, without knowledge the soul is not good, and he who hurries with his feet sins" - in these words: "our Sages taught: one commandment leads to another commandment, and one transgression leads to another transgression; a person should not grieve over transgressions he committed unwittingly, but [understand] that a door has been opened for him to sin even willfully; and a person should not rejoice over a commandment that comes to his hand, but [understand] that many commandments are destined to come to his hand. Therefore, if a person sins unwittingly, of him it is said, 'and he who hurries with his feet sins'" - to this point.

This is the aspect of the fear of sin - that one should distance himself from sin and fear it, for sin is the evil, the turbidity and refuse of holiness, and is a term of deficiency, as in (I Kings 1:21), "I and my son Solomon will be [regarded as] sinners [chata'im]" - for the husks are deficient in the supernal light. For this reason one must fear that a door will be opened for him to further transgressions, for "one corresponding to the other God has made" (Ecclesiastes 7:14) - just as one who performs the commandments cleaves ever more to the supernal spirituality the more he performs, so too one who commits transgressions cleaves to transgressions, in such a way that from an unwitting act he comes to a willful one.

As for the reason it says "if a person sins unwittingly, of him it is said, 'and he who hurries with his feet sins'" - our Sages, of blessed memory, said similarly at the end of the third chapter of Yoma (39a), on "do not defile yourselves through them, lest you become defiled through them" (Leviticus 11:43) [homiletically read without the Aleph, "ve-nitmetem" as "ve-nitamtem," you become dulled/stopped up]: "a person who defiles himself a little, they defile him a great deal." And the same applies to the matter of holiness, as they said there: a person who sanctifies himself a little, they sanctify him a great deal.

The matter is this: the soul within a person and the matter of the Torah's commandments as they have become physical follow the same pattern. For the soul within the human body is constricted, similar to how the Holy One, blessed be He, constricted His Shechinah between the poles of the Ark - for above, the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him, and yet, for the love of Israel and their benefit, He constricted His Shechinah there. So too the soul: above, before it was clothed in this world, it shines without limit, greater than the angels, since its emanation and hewing is from the Throne of Glory, as they say, "the souls are hewn from the Throne of Glory." And just as every level of the Throne is great compared to everything beneath it, as we explained in chapter two, so too the souls hewn from it - especially if it is a soul of Atzilut, which shines ever more and encompasses with its light everything beneath it. And we already know that the soul is likened to the Holy One, blessed be He: just as the Holy One, blessed be He, sees and is not seen, so too the souls, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Berachot 10a). And so our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 8a): to what are the souls of the righteous, before the Shechinah, compared? To candles before a torch. And with this we may understand what is said in the Zohar (Emor 103b), that the souls of the Patriarchs, and Moses and Aaron, Joseph and David, come to every single sukkah of Israel [on Sukkot] - and how is this conceivable, if not in the manner described? We find, then, that the soul, within this coarse human body, is constricted in a way that is not its natural manner.

And in this same manner it happened with the Torah and the commandments: for every single commandment, above, is a supernal light cleaving to the Tree of Life, for a commandment is "the LORD," as is explained in the Tikkunim (131b) and Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas 228b). But through the sin of the first man, and likewise through the sin of the [golden] calf, the Torah and the commandments became physical, and a person now performs a physical commandment, such as wearing a tallit with tzitzit, or leather tefillin, and so on for the other commandments. My teacher, peace be upon him, elaborated on this discourse in many places.

And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (4a) concerning the vowel-points - that below they appear small to us, while above they shine without limit, like the sun, which appears small to us but is many times larger than the earth. And likewise concerning the letters, it is explained in Parashat Acharei Mot (73a) that upon the thorn [tip] of the supernal Yud hang many worlds, in these words: "one thousand four hundred and fifty myriads of worlds all hang upon the thorn of the Alef," and the other worlds hang upon the body of the Alef itself - see there.

We find, then, that when a person now performs the physical commandment, and it appears in his eyes a small thing, in the eyes of the Holy One, blessed be He, it is very great - for in performing the physical commandment he arouses its spiritual root above, and its spirituality above has no measure or limit; therefore they said, "they sanctify him a great deal," without measure.

Similarly, it is explained in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 5), in these words: "let no good deed you do for His Name seem small in your eyes, even a word or a glance, for what is little from you is much before Him" - and likewise regarding transgressions. And the closest analogy for this is the movement of the sun over the earth: a measure of a cubit's movement corresponds to many miles' movement in the [celestial] sphere; and likewise the movement of a shadow on an astrolabe" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 4:53-5:8: With this we may understand why the Holy One, blessed be He, needs to reward a person by appointing over each commandment many thousands upon thousands of angels, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Pekudei 244b-262b) concerning the holy Heichalot [Palaces]. The reason is that the supernal light of that commandment's spirituality shines forth through all those small chambers. And if you ask, would it not suffice for there to be a single angel? We answer: it is impossible for the supernal light to shine forth in a single angel, for then that angel would be found equal in stature to the spirituality of the commandment itself in its own place, and would itself be the commandment - and this is not the intent; rather, the light shines forth into vessels through which the soul may derive pleasure. Nevertheless, there is one principal angel in whom the primary light of the commandment resides, and beneath him many thousands who receive the remaining sparks of light.

From this we come to understand the matter of impurity: for when a person transgresses a single commandment of our holy Torah, such as eating forbidden fat or blood and the like, this thing, below, is physical and appears to the transgressor a small matter; but above it is impurity without measure - for according to the spiritual ascent of the commandment [when fulfilled], so is the measure of the descent of impurity [when transgressed], through many angels of destruction. Therefore it is explained [in the Zohar] that many bundles of impure spirits seize hold of the soul, as it says regarding the chambers of impurity several times (see Miketz 200a), and likewise "many wardens of the law" (263b, 265a) - for the great impurity, which is the matter of that great judgment, must be divided among all those forces to judge the soul, so that it can receive its punishment through each and every one of them.

We find, then, in this a reason for a person to distance himself from evil, which is sin, and to fear lest it come to his hand even unwittingly, because of the disgrace of the sin and the impurity within it - and instead to cleave to the good, which is the good that endures forever and for all eternity, "that it may go well with you," for the world that is entirely good and the world that is entirely long [everlasting].

This chapter will explain the ways of fear from the aspect of the blemish that reaches above, to the Shechinah, and [will discuss] distancing oneself from the enticements of the evil inclination and drawing near to the good.

Our Sages, of blessed memory, said, cited in the Yalkut, Parashat Chukat (remez 768), on the verse (Numbers 21:34), "and the LORD said to Moses, fear him not" - in these words: "this is what Scripture says (Proverbs 28:14), 'happy is the man who fears always' - such is the quality of the righteous: even though the Holy One, blessed be He, reassures them, they do not cast off fear from themselves. And so of Jacob it is written (Genesis 32:8), 'and Jacob was greatly afraid' - why was he afraid? He said, perhaps I have become sullied in some way while with Laban; and it is written (Deuteronomy 23:15), 'and He shall see no unseemly thing among you, and turn away from you' - and the Holy One, blessed be He, left me [i.e., protected him]. Even Moses seized upon fear - why was he afraid? He said, perhaps Israel transgressed in the war against Sichon, or became sullied through transgression; He said to him, 'fear him not'" - to the extent relevant here.

According to the plain sense that appears from this passage: "and He shall see no unseemly thing among you" means no defiling matter, that is, the stain of some sin; "and turn away from you" means that the Shechinah would depart from him. And what is meant by "why was he afraid" may be understood from what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 4a): "Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi raised a contradiction: it is written (Genesis 28:15), 'and behold, I am with you, and I will keep you wherever you go,' yet it is written (32:8), 'and Jacob was greatly afraid' - he was afraid lest sin be caused" - and the explanation of "lest sin be caused" is the matter of "perhaps I have become sullied in some way while with Laban," and so on, as written.

However, in the Zohar (Acharei Mot 75a-b) it is explained that "an unseemly thing" [ervat davar] refers to the Shechinah, in these words: "Rabbi Shimon opened [with the verse], 'for the LORD your God walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you,' and so on (Deuteronomy 23:15) - 'for the LORD your God' - this is the Shechinah, who is found among Israel, and all the more so in exile, to shield them always from every side, and from all the other nations, idol worshippers, so that they should not destroy Israel; for it is taught, the wicked of Israel's [own nation] cannot harm them until Israel weaken the strength of the Shechinah before the great appointed [angelic] princes of the other nations - then the wicked of Israel are able to prevail over them and rule over them and decree upon them many evil decrees. And when they repent to receive her, she breaks the strength and power of all those great appointed princes, and breaks the strength and power of the wicked of Israel, and exacts full payment from them all. Therefore, 'and your camp shall be holy' - for a person must not defile himself with his sins and transgress the words of the Torah, for if he does so, they defile him, as it is written (Leviticus 11:43), 've-nitmetem bam' [without the Aleph, 've-nitamtem,' you become dulled] - and we have learned, two hundred forty-eight limbs are in the body, and they all become defiled when he becomes defiled - that is, when he intends to become defiled. Therefore, 'and your camp shall be holy' - what is 'your camp'? These are the limbs of the body. 'And He shall see no unseemly thing among you' - the nakedness/blemish of this matter [davar], as we have established; for if this happens, then certainly 'and turn away from you.' And therefore, 'the nakedness of your father's wife you shall not uncover' - why? Because it is written, 'it is your father's nakedness,' as we have established" - to this point.

We have learned: for three things Israel is delayed [from redemption] in exile - because they treat the Shechinah with contempt in exile, and turn their faces away from the Shechinah, and defile themselves before the Shechinah; and all of this we have established in our own teaching - to this point.

Now, in general, four aspects of the matter of the blemish are mentioned in this passage. The first is that when Israel sins, they weaken the strength of the Shechinah before the seventy [heavenly] princes; and this is the Shechinah's complaint (Song of Songs 1:6), "they made me keeper of the vineyards" - these being the seventy princes - "but my own vineyard," which is Israel, "I have not kept." Therefore it says (Deuteronomy 23:15), "for the LORD your God walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you and to give up your enemies before you," and so on; but when a person causes a blemish, she does not deliver, but rather, Heaven forfend, the opposite - of her it is said (ibid. 32:18), "you have forgotten the Rock who bore you," as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained, which I cited in chapter three.

Similarly, Rashbi, of blessed memory, said (Vayetze 152b), on the verse (Proverbs 24:10), "if you faint in the day of adversity, your strength is small [tzar koach-cha]" - in these words: "'if you faint' - if he lets his hands go slack from Torah; 'in the day of adversity, your strength is small' - what is 'tzar koach-cha'? [It may be read as] 'tzar koach Kah' [restricted is the power of Kah, i.e., the Name Yud-Heh] - for it [this power] is always at his right, and its protection is always over a person when he walks in the ways of the Torah, and then it pushes the evil away from him, so that it should not draw near him and should not be able to accuse him. But when a person strays from the ways of the Torah and lets his hands go slack from it, then 'the power of Kah is restricted,' because the evil, which is on the left, rules over the person and pushes this 'Kah' outward, until it is forced into a tight place" - to this point.

The second and third aspects concerning the blemish are "and your camp shall be holy" and "and He shall see no unseemly thing among you." The matter is this: when a person causes a blemish above, he darkens that light in the aspect of that limb with which he sinned, and mercy withdraws from there and judgment prevails; therefore that blemish must be discharged below - whether by afflicting him with suffering in his body or his wealth, or that darkness and judgment are kept in store to be discharged upon his soul, by its entering the fire of Gehinnom, where it will be refined and receive that entire judgment in the measure of what it blemished; and this is [the meaning of] (Leviticus 24:20), "as he has inflicted a blemish on a person, so shall it be inflicted on him" - and "a person" [adam] refers to the supernal Adam.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:22-33: Further, it may be like the matter explained (Tikkunei Zohar 146b): "'honor your father and your mother' - your father, this is the Holy One, blessed be He; your mother, this is the Shechinah. Fear of her is through the negative commandments; honoring her is through the positive commandments - of these it is said, 'for those who honor Me I will honor'; and likewise all those who transgress the negative commandments, of them it is said, 'and those who scorn Me shall be lightly esteemed'" - to the extent relevant here. We find, then, according to this, that the disgrace of the Shechinah is that they do not accord her the honor due to her through the positive commandments, and they transgress the negative commandments. Now, in all matters where a person is obligated in the honor of his earthly father and mother, he is likewise obligated in the honor of the supernal Father and Mother; and just as one is warned not to demean the honor of one's earthly father and mother, and stands under a curse - as it is said (Deuteronomy 27:16), "cursed be he who demeans his father or his mother" - and Rambam wrote (Hilchot Mamrim, chapter 5) that this applies even by a mere gesture - so too one must be careful not to demean the honor of the supernal Father and Mother, and to be careful of everything pertaining to their honor. Of this sort, it appears, one must be careful of what Rashbi said (Terumah 131b; see the Additions 256a), that one who speaks in the synagogue causes disgrace in the supernal arrangement above.

The second, "and turn their faces away from the Shechinah," has a general aspect and a particular aspect. The general aspect is like [the actions of] the wicked, who turn back and turn their faces away from the Shechinah, saying with their mouths that they do not wish to have any portion in the God of Israel. The particular aspect is one who breaks off from words of Torah for idle matters, because one who occupies himself with Torah has his face toward the Shechinah, as our Sages, of blessed memory, expounded (Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 18; see Tamid 32b), on the verse (Lamentations 2:19), "pour out your heart like water before the presence of the LORD" - and he breaks off; he is found to have turned his face away from the Shechinah. Similarly, one who prays and breaks off in the middle, even if it is during the [Psalms of] praise, and especially if it is during the silent Amidah, and in the middle of his prayer turns his face to look here and there for his own needs - certainly this touches upon the honor of the Shechinah.

The third, "and they defile themselves before the Shechinah" - one must be careful in this regard of everything the Torah explicitly calls impurity: the impurity of forbidden foods, as it is said (Leviticus 11:43), "do not make yourselves detestable with any swarming thing that swarms, and do not defile yourselves with them, lest you become defiled through them"; the impurity of forbidden relations (ibid. 18:24), "do not defile yourselves with any of these things, for the nations that I am casting out before you defiled themselves with all these things," and so on; and one must be careful of the impurity of menstrual separation.

The impurity of leprous plagues [tzara'at] - our Sages, of blessed memory, explained that plagues come as a result of the sin of slander (Arachin 16a). And Rashbi explained (Metzora 53a): "Rabbi Chiya said: whoever utters slander, all his limbs become defiled," and so on. And in Parashat Shemini (41a) he said: "a person should not blemish his mouth and his tongue, and how much more so should he not defile his own soul and body, for he becomes defiled thereby in the other world" - to this point.

Also, the impurity of idolatry, as it is said (Deuteronomy 7:26), "you shall utterly detest it, and utterly abhor it." What bears on this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Tetzaveh 182a) - and I shall cite his words below - that one who is angry defiles himself, within and without, like idolatry itself; and of one who is angry it is said (Exodus 34:17), "you shall not make for yourself molten gods" - meaning that he literally makes himself into idolatry. And likewise one who is haughty, and similarly, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Mechilta, Parashat Yitro), on the verse (Exodus 20:18), "and Moses drew near to the thick darkness" - in these words: "and whoever is haughty of heart causes the defilement of the land and the withdrawal of the Shechinah, as it is said (Psalms 101:5), 'one who has a haughty eye and a proud heart, him I cannot endure'; and all who are haughty of heart are called an abomination, as it is said (Proverbs 16:5), 'every haughty heart is an abomination to the LORD.' Idolatry is called an abomination, as it is said (Deuteronomy 7:26), 'and you shall not bring an abomination into your house' - just as idolatry defiles the land and causes the Shechinah to withdraw," and so on - to this point.

Also, one must be careful of the impurity of emitting seed in vain, for this sin blemishes the Shechinah, and therefore it says "before the Shechinah." And Rashbi explained (Vayeshev 188a) that there is no sin by which a person defiles himself more than one who emits seed in vain, in these words: "come and see - of all the sins by which a person defiles himself in this world, this is the sin by which a person is defiled the most, in this world and in the World to Come: one who spills his seed uselessly, and emits seed in vain, by hand or by foot, and defiles himself through it - as it is written (Psalms 5:5), 'for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You.' Therefore, he does not enter behind the curtain and does not see the countenance of the Ancient of Days, as we have learned. Here it is written 'evil shall not sojourn with You,' and it is written (Genesis 38:7), 'and Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD'; and therefore it is written (Isaiah 1:15), 'your hands are full of blood.' Happy is the portion of the person who fears his Master and keeps himself from the evil way, and purifies himself to occupy himself with the fear of his Master" - to this point.

There is yet another impurity, although the Torah does not explicitly call it impurity, and it is one who has relations with his wife not in the natural manner; and the Zohar, Parashat Pekudei (259a), is stringent about this, in these words: "concerning this we have learned: whoever has relations with his bed from the rear weakens the arrangement of face-to-face gazing, which is meant to illuminate everything together and for everything to be found face-to-face, in fitting union - as it is said (Genesis 2:24), 'and he shall cleave to his wife' - to his wife specifically, and not to the back of his wife" - to this point.

In these three matters, the word "Shechinah" is mentioned in each and every one, because she is called "Shechinah" [dwelling] on account of her dwelling among the lower beings, specifically among Israel, as it says (Exodus 34:9), "let my Lord, please, go in our midst" - and as our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (see Berachot 7a): he asked that the Shechinah rest upon Israel and not upon the idolatrous nations, and the Holy One, blessed be He, agreed. Whoever transgresses one of these matters, behold, the Shechinah is against him and he has no shame of face, and he causes the prolonging of the exile - for Israel was not exiled until they said, "we have no portion in David... every man to his tents, O Israel" (see II Chronicles 10:16) - do not read "le-ohalecha" [to your tents] but "le-Elohecha" [to your gods] (see Yalkut Shmuel, remez 106; Tanchuma, Beshalach 16) - and they denied the God of Israel. And one who sins in the matters mentioned is like one who denies [divine] providence, and was not chastised in exile in proportion to being the cause of the exile; therefore it is fitting, Heaven forfend, that he should be further delayed in exile.

Let us return to the discourse we began at the start of the chapter, that one must fear not to blemish the Shechinah - this being the "unseemly thing" we explained. There are yet two more aspects concerning the blemish to her, explained in the Tikkunim and in Ra'aya Meheimna.

In the Tikkunim (49b) it is said that the heart is the Shechinah, and there are two chambers in the heart, one the dwelling of the good inclination and the other the dwelling of the evil inclination; and it says that the good inclination is the Shechinah, in the aspects we shall explain, in these words: "'the heart understands, the heart knows, the heart sees' - this is the Shechinah, who takes only what is pure, which is a clean offering of prayer, without bran and without refuse, and she draws near to her husband, the beauty of all. But the lobe of the liver gives her husband only remnants and refuse - and who is her husband? The spleen - 'another god' [el acher] - and from these remnants taken from her, dark and black spleen-blood is made, and this is the deceitful serpent that seduced Eve, who is the heart, and caused her death. And behold, there are two chambers of the heart - which of them does he seduce? Rather, the one on the left, of which it is said (Ecclesiastes 10:2), 'a fool's heart is to his left,' and of which it is said (ibid. 7:26), 'and I find more bitter than death, the woman.' 'A wise man's heart is to his right' - this is the woman of valor, the crown of her husband, of whom it is said (Proverbs 18:22), 'he who finds a wife finds good' - for she is the good inclination, a person's good fortune, of whom it is said (Ezekiel 44:30), 'to cause a blessing to rest on your house' - 'the blessing of the LORD, it enriches' (Proverbs 10:22) - and of her it is said (Ecclesiastes 9:9), 'enjoy life with the wife whom you love'" - to the extent relevant here.

The intent that emerges from the totality of his words, without examining his language too closely, is that "heart" used plainly refers to the Shechinah, and she has two chambers: one on the right side, the dwelling of Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at; and the other on the left side, for the nursing of the judgment of Gevurah - and it is from the left side that the fool clings to his portion below, for all the external [husks] are found below, on the left side, in the sequence of the levels descending. This is [the meaning of] "a wise man's heart is to his right, and a fool's heart is to his left" - for one who wishes to become wise should go to the right, for it is specifically to his right that wisdom comes to him. And her being the dwelling of Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at is alluded to by his bringing three verses: the first, corresponding to Da'at, which is in the middle - "this is the woman of valor, the crown of her husband" - and this is a person's "mazal" [fortune/influx], as is explained in the Tikkunim (99b), in these words: "the supernal Vav, which is the supernal mazal that rises in thought." And corresponding to Binah, it is said, "to cause a blessing to rest on your house; the blessing of the LORD, it enriches" - and it is explained in the Tikkunim (27a) that this is Binah. And corresponding to Chochmah, which is life, it says, "enjoy life with the wife whom you love," for love is on the right. And although above I explained, in the name of Rashbi, that the good inclination in general is on the right - the intent there is the right arm, which comprises three joints, namely Chochmah, Binah, and Da'at, as is explained in the Idra (Naso 142a-b); and one may learn what is unclear from what is made explicit.

With this we may understand a second explanation of the passage we cited from Parashat Bereshit concerning fear: "why is it called the fear of the LORD? because it is the Tree of Good and Evil," and so on. With this it is explained, for it is the secret of the heart, the dwelling of the good, which is the right; and evil is the secret of judgment, and evil itself extends downward in the sequence of the descending levels. If a person merits, he cleaves to her in the aspect of her right side, which is the good inclination, in the aspects mentioned; if he does not merit, behold, evil cleaves to him, in the secret of "a fool's heart is to his left."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 5:9-21: Now, to arouse a person to repent, they defile him and place upon him a blemish corresponding to the nakedness and the blemish he inflicted upon the "matter" [davar], which is the Shechinah; and this is [the meaning of] "he shall not see [lo yera'eh]," meaning that the blemish and nakedness you inflicted upon the "matter" should not be visible upon your body, but rather "your camp shall be holy" - that all two hundred forty-eight of his limbs should be holy, meaning that they should all be unified as one, to the point that we could say of them all that they are together a single, holy limb.

The matter is this: when a person causes a blemish even in a single limb, it is accounted as though he blemished the entire stature, for all two hundred forty-eight limbs are unified as one; therefore, even if he sinned with only a single limb, all two hundred forty-eight of his limbs are defiled. And this is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, said: "two hundred forty-eight limbs in a single body, and they all become defiled."

With this we may understand, in a second way, what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 39a): "a person who defiles himself a little, they defile him a great deal" - meaning that even though he sinned with only a single limb, they defile all two hundred forty-eight of his limbs a great deal. And likewise regarding "and your camp shall be holy": "one who sanctifies himself a little, they sanctify him a great deal" - for even though he sanctified only a single limb, all two hundred forty-eight limbs, which are "your camp" in the plural, are sanctified with supernal holiness - "holy" [kadosh] in the singular, as I explained - just as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (see Kiddushin 39b): whoever performs a commandment as it is stated merits life in the World to Come.

The fourth blemish is "and turn away from you," and this matter may be explained as it is explained at the end of Parashat Noach (76a) concerning the Shechinah - that when a person is blemished, the Shechinah withdraws from him. And so it is said in the Tikkunim (52b), in these words: "and if the soul becomes soiled with sins, or lacks even a single one of those commandments - as the masters of the Mishnah established, 'a transgression extinguishes a commandment' - in the place where the transgression rests and the commandment has withdrawn from it, that limb is blemished, and this is the soul's defect; because of it the Holy One, blessed be He, does not rest upon the soul. This is [the meaning of] (Leviticus 21:18), 'any man who has a defect shall not draw near' - a soul that has a defect in its two hundred forty-eight commandments does not draw near to Him because of it" - to the extent relevant here.

In this manner one may explain the verse here: "for the LORD your God walks," and so on. For it is the way of the Shechinah to walk before a person to guard him, as is explained in Parashat Shelach Lecha (166a); and it is the way of a person to walk behind the Shechinah, as it says (Deuteronomy 13:5), "after the LORD your God shall you walk." And when a person causes a blemish, she withdraws from before him and turns to his rear, so that he is left with no protection before him.

However, what appears from the language brought afterward - "and therefore, 'the nakedness of your father's wife you shall not uncover,' why? because it is written, 'it is your father's nakedness'" - explains that the blemish reaches Tiferet as well. If so, it appears that this too is alluded to in the verse, just as "an unseemly thing" [ervat davar] was mentioned: namely, "the nakedness of your father's wife" also alludes to "it is your father's nakedness," in the words "and turn away from you."

The matter is that when the Shechinah is blemished because of a person's sin, Tiferet withdraws from her, because she is a throne for him, and he does not rest upon an incomplete throne - as is explained in Parashat Vayikra (4b), and likewise in the Tikkunim, concerning "and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and went outside" [Genesis 39:12].

Similarly, it is explained in the Tikkunim (146b), in these words: "in this manner the Holy One, blessed be He, drives away the Shechinah and casts her out of His house - this is [the meaning of] (Isaiah 50:1), 'and for your transgressions your mother was sent away.' And is it not so that whoever honors her in exile honors the Holy One, blessed be He, and whoever demeans her demeans the Holy One, blessed be He? And therefore (I Samuel 2:30), 'for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who scorn Me shall be lightly esteemed'" - to this point. The reason for this is that the two of them are two aspects of one countenance, and a king without a queen is not [truly] a king, as Rashbi explained (Vayikra 5a): "'great is the LORD and highly praised, in the city of our God, His holy mountain' (Psalms 48:2) - it is heard that a king without a queen is not a king, and is not great, and is not praised" - to this point. And so it is likewise explained in Ra'aya Meheimna (Mishpatim 117b): "the disgrace of the Matrona [Queen] is when they demean her place, and this is the disgrace of the Matrona" - to this point. What is meant by "the disgrace of the Matrona is when they demean her place" will be explained, with God's help, in the matter of the blemish of the Throne.

What is meant by "and turn away from you" is explained by Rashbi (Shelach 165a): "if he is a pious, holy person, who keeps the covenant properly, He places him behind [Him] and He is in front; and if you say, [what of] one who keeps the rear? Behold, greater and more supernal is the protection of one who keeps it [the covenant fully] - and who is he? The supernal righteous one [tzaddik], who enters with abundant love between 'righteous' [tzaddik] and 'righteousness' [tzedek], and is found protected on every side; happy is he who keeps this covenant" - to this point. And further there (166a) it is proven that when a person is righteous, he walks behind the Shechinah, because the Shechinah walks before him to guard him, as it is written (Exodus 23:20), "behold, I send an angel before you, to guard you" - and the person stands at the level of the righteous one, so that he is behind her; and this is [the meaning of] "after the LORD your God shall you walk." And what they said (see the Zohar, on Berachot 61a), "a man should not walk behind a woman" - the meaning is that he should not descend below into the world of the female, as with Abraham, of whom it is said (Genesis 17:1), "walk before Me" - and it is explained there that this was because he had neither circumcision nor the uncovering [of the corona], and this is a deficiency; for [of Saul, similarly] "he has turned back from following Me" (I Samuel 15:11) means that he descended from the level of the male; and this is what is said there: "he was not behind, because he was not uncovered" - see there. With this we may understand "and turn away from you": that the male, who walks behind you to guard you, withdraws from you because you caused the blemishing of his female counterpart.

We may also say that "achareicha" [behind you/after you] refers to the Shechinah, who is called "achor" [rear], as it says (Exodus 33:23), "and you shall see My back [achorai]" - and Tiferet turns away from her because of the blemish. But the first explanation appears to me the primary one.

However, one may combine both explanations as one, and say: certainly it is never possible to separate the [divine] unity; for although it is said (Deuteronomy 23:15), "the LORD your God" - this is the Shechinah (in the Zohar mentioned, 75a) - Tiferet is present there as well, as it says, "the LORD, He is God" (ibid. 4:35). Therefore it says, "for the LORD your God walks," and so on - both together, in unity, walk, and so on; and therefore it says, "to deliver you and to give up your enemies," and so on - a double protection corresponding to both of them. And it is explained above that she is called "the guarding of the way," and Tiferet comes to guard her, as it says (Isaiah 42:8), "I am the LORD, that is My Name, and My glory I will not give to another." And since he comes to guard her, his face is toward her back, in the manner of a guard who follows from behind; and Israel is in between, as it says, "whoever keeps the covenant enters between 'righteous' and 'righteousness.'" And what is meant by "his face is toward her back" is the face of mercy and good providence, to bestow flow upon her - for "back" [achor] indicates withdrawal and concealment; the proof is Adam and Eve, who, when they were back to back, there was no union. Here, in the matter of guarding, there is no union but rather a manner of flow; therefore he was commanded not to blemish the Shechinah, lest he cause the withdrawal of Tiferet from her, and cause Him to turn His face from her, so that they would be back to back - and this is "and turn away from you," stated plainly, referring both to the Shechinah, who is called "back," and to the person, who is in between, whose back is to the male. Thus four aspects of the matter of the blemish have been explained.

We have seen fit to complete the explanation of this passage, since it bears on our discussion of the blemishing of the Shechinah. It says that for three things Israel is delayed in exile; it says "delayed" because the exile of the Shechinah was decreed for only a thousand years, as it is said (Lamentations 1:13), "He has made me desolate, faint all the day" - and so it is explained in Parashat Va'era (Zohar, Shemot Rabbah context, 17a).

The first is "because they treat the Shechinah with contempt in exile" - meaning that they profane the Name of the LORD, as it is said (Ezekiel 36:20), "when they said of them, these are the people of the LORD, yet they have gone out of His land." When Israel does something involving the profanation of the Name, there is no greater disgrace to the Shechinah than this - a parable of a father who has a son, and the son does improper things to people, so that people say, cursed is he who bore this one, cursed is he who raised this one. This applies generally to the whole nation, and in particular to every single individual of Israel who transgresses what the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded him - he causes disgrace above to the Shechinah, for Scripture says (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother was sent away." And when a person adds transgression, he adds exile and banishment, for above they say: see the mother, what kind of children she raised! It is fitting, Heaven forfend, that she be banished outside the palace, since she did not discipline her son to be proper - and similarly our Sages, of blessed memory, explained (Yalkut Bereshit, remez 8, and see remez 27) concerning the nine curses with which the earth was cursed (Tikkunei Zohar 95b).
